title: The mosque of palm trunks
hookLine: in Medina the Prophet's Mosque is built of mud brick and palm, and he carries bricks

cards: Today in Medina, the Prophet's Mosque is vast: white marble, a forest of columns, a green dome over his grave, pilgrims from all over the world. Strip it back to the first version.
A patch of ground where dates were laid out to dry. Walls of sun-dried mud brick. Tree trunks for pillars.
Palm branches for a roof, which leaked when it rained. A floor of bare earth. And among the people carrying the bricks, sweating in the heat, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself.
Today: the mosque of palm trunks.

teach.b: The story is in Sahih al-Bukhari. When the Prophet reached the center of Medina, the land where his camel knelt belonged to two orphan boys. They offered it to him as a gift; he insisted on paying for it.
The plot had some palm trees and some old graves.

teach.h: TRUNKS FOR PILLARS, PALM FOR A ROOF.
teach.b: The trees were cut down, and their trunks lined up as pillars. The walls went up in mud brick, and the roof was palm leaves laid over beams.

The companions carried the bricks, chanting a short rhyming verse as they worked, and the Prophet carried bricks with them and chanted along. It was built plainly, and on purpose. It had to be: there was no money.
But even later, when there was, the mosque stayed simple for a long time.

A bare floor under a palm-leaf roof, so when it rained, people prayed in mud. A hadith even describes the Prophet rising from prostration at the dawn prayer one Ramadan with mud and water on his forehead.
And one palm trunk has its own story. Before there was a pulpit, the Prophet used to lean against a trunk when he gave the Friday sermon.
When a small wooden pulpit was built and he stepped up onto it, Sahih al-Bukhari says the trunk cried out, like a child, and the Prophet came down and put his hand on it until it quieted.
The Prophet's Mosque began as mud, palm and earth.
Everything that came later was built on that.

how: Muslims hold the Prophet's Mosque in Medina among their holiest places, and pilgrims visit it; many local mosques are simple rooms, often with carpets on the floor and no furniture.

o: the Medina mosque first built of mud and palm
any mosque where the Prophet once prayed
the Ka'ba, the shrine at the center of Mecca

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: cried when he left it for a pulpit

s: the orphans' land was taken as a gift
they offered it free; the Prophet insisted on paying.
the Prophet's Mosque first had a floor of bare earth
when rain came through the palm roof, people prayed in mud.
the Prophet supervised while others carried the bricks
he carried bricks too, and chanted along with the builders.

games.q: two orphan boys offer you their land for the new mosque, free. you're the leader of the whole community. what do you do?
o: insist on paying them for it.
games.why: he insisted on paying the orphans. the hadith doesn't give his reason; some readers see care for orphans in it.

practice: If you can, sit on the floor for this, with no cushion, or just a thin one, and feel how close you are to the ground. In that first mosque, people prayed on bare earth, shoulder to shoulder.
Notice what it's like to have nothing between you and the floor but your own clothes, and let it be plain.

wordCard.voice: Prophet's Mosque. The first building in Medina: mud brick walls, palm-trunk pillars, and a roof of palm leaves.

orig.note: Arabic: the Prophet's Mosque, in Medina.

carryVoice: Your line: built plainly. Mud brick, palm trunks, and a roof that leaked. Day two hundred fifty-eight, done.
